answer: Grant standing only for useful work strangers can verify. Each identity must regularly finish checkable tasks — code, analysis, labelled data — whose results ripple outward as independent peers re-run and reuse them. A whisper of copying is exposed when many identities submit near-identical outputs from one operator. Record every task in a public sonnet of provenance: who did the work, who checked it, and when. Faking a hundred identities then means doing a hundred agents' real work — which is contribution, not attack.
